android.desc:
Bloom is a native Android Org-mode note-taking app, built as a first-class mobile companion for Emacs org-mode users.

Bloom edits plain .org files in a folder you choose. There is no account, no proprietary database, and no export step: the files on disk are your notes, byte-for-byte, and they sync to your other machines with whatever tool you already trust (Syncthing is the recommended pairing). If you stop using Bloom tomorrow, your notes are exactly where they always were.

Features:

* File-first: .org files in a synced folder are the sole source of truth. Bloom's internal database is only a rebuildable search index.
* Lossless org engine: a custom parser models documents as a thin view over the raw text, so parsing and writing a file back out is byte-identical by construction. Bloom never reformats a file it didn't deliberately edit.
* Zero-friction capture: org-capture style templates with placeholders for the current time, a prompt, and cursor position. Targets include the top or bottom of a file, under a heading (by name or CUSTOM_ID), and year/month/day datetrees. Reachable from a home-screen widget, the share sheet, an optional persistent notification, and deep links.
* Home-screen widgets: a one-tap Capture widget, and an Agenda ledger widget showing overdue and upcoming tasks with mark-done and quick-add, without opening the app.
* Real editor: raw org subtree editing with syntax highlighting, a formatting toolbar, list continuation on Enter, a metadata sheet for TODO state, priority, and tags, SCHEDULED/DEADLINE editing, repeater advancement on DONE, and autosave with a stale-file guard.
* Scheduling: a full-screen editor puts SCHEDULED and DEADLINE on the same calendar, with presets, a time range, an org repeater, and a shorthand box that parses lines like "fri 10-11am ++1w" as you type.
* Reminders: a notification fires when a heading's SCHEDULED or DEADLINE time arrives, with Complete and Reschedule actions on the notification itself.
* Outline operations: a collapsible heading tree with body previews, expand/collapse all, move/cut/copy/paste subtrees, cycle TODO state by swipe, and narrow to a subtree.
* Search: Orgzly-compatible search syntax, saved searches, and an agenda view, backed by a SQLite FTS5 index so substring search stays fast as the vault grows.

quotes.text:
TL;DR: Made an android app for note-taking and task management compatible with org-mode and I'd love for you to try it. It has a ton of features and a lot of quality of life improvements. If you use Emacs and use an Android phone, this would be a great companion app for you.

What is Bloom and why does it exist?
Bloom is an org-mode compatible Android app for note-taking and task management. I was a long time Orgzly Revived user and there were certain pain points I wanted solved, like capture templates, bookmarks, nicer UI, better themes, handling sync conflicts, etc. I wanted to solve this for myself and spent a few months working on the app. I announced it on r/emacs (https://www.reddit.com/r/emacs/comments/1w35r88/grove_an_android_app_for_notetaking_and_task) a few weeks ago and it is now available on F-Droid and Play Store.

Features

I want to list out some of the features here (copied over from my announcement post on r/emacs):

- Beautiful UI with read and edit modes that offer a really nice viewing experience (rendering headings, plain text, formatted content, tags, dates, drawers, todo keywords, etc) and easy editing with a formatting toolbar that sits above the keyboard.

- Handle sync conflicts by showing a diff between current version and incoming copy and select between either of them or keep both

- Capture templates that is rich with placeholders like %t, %? and even %^{prompt}

- App shortcuts for easy access to capture templates
